new.x: The IT Act, 2000 introduced all three concepts: electronic record (legally recognised under Sec. 4), digital signature (Sec. 3 and 5) and Certifying Authority (licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates). Options leaving out any one of them are wrong (MPPSC 2021 PYQ: 'all of the above').
new.tq: IT Act 2000 concepts = e-record + digital signature + CA (all three).

new.s: In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), the Supreme Court read down Section 79 of the IT Act. As a result, 'actual knowledge' that obliges an intermediary to take down content means:
o: Any complaint received from a private user
A court order or a notice from the appropriate Government
Knowledge gained through the intermediary's own monitoring
An advisory issued by CERT-In alone
new.x: The Court read down Sec. 79 so that 'actual knowledge' means a court order or a government notice. A private user complaint does not by itself trigger loss of safe harbour; intermediaries are not expected to judge content on their own monitoring; a CERT-In advisory is not the stated trigger. The same judgment struck down Sec. 66A and upheld Sec. 69A.
new.tq: Sec 79 actual knowledge = court order or govt notice (Shreya Singhal).
